violations: CURRENT_TREE_UNCOVERED: tests/test_git_object_reader.py (absent from the evidence manifest although it exists at the baseline -> pre-existing)
red.root_cause: tools/build_evidence_manifest.py::iter_files() globs ROOT.rglob('*') and excludes only .git, __pycache__, .pyc/.db and the manifest+seal. Regenerating the manifest for this round would sweep in the round's live Codex homes (lane/writer-home, lane/checker-home - the latter contains auth.json) and the 9,674 container artefacts under ao/out (162 MB, including reproducible venvs), listing their paths and hashes in a committed file. That is why the R5 round left the check red too, and it is the reason a reseal must first relocate that scratch out of the product tree.
fix_sequence: move lane/writer-home, lane/checker-home and the container venv/scratch trees out of .hgk/rounds/R5P-... (keep the four AO verdict JSONs and the v2/v3/v4 raw runs the verdicts cite)
python tools/build_evidence_manifest.py --seal  (manifest + seal regenerated over a clean tree)
rebuild the R5P sidecar via tools/publication_attestation.py + ops/bind_r5p_checker_identity.py so its source_manifest_seal matches the new seal
commit, push, read back - and this is a new subject, so the AO pass is invalidated for it

red.note: the round's bound product digest counts 288 files over PRODUCT_ROOTS (worktree bytes, LF-normalised), while the publication tool's product_digest counts its own PRODUCT_PREFIXES over git blobs. The two are different rules, disclosed in evidence/PUBLICATION_BINDING_R5P.json; an officer must not equate them.
the shipped wheel is member-identical but not byte-identical when rebuilt by another ZIP creator; the committed wheel sha is the binding.
